title: Represented Is Not Computed: A Causal Test of Candidate Algorithmic Intermediates in a Transformer
abstract: arXiv:2605.22488v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Structured prompts require integrating components according to task-relevant relations. How a network implements this integration is often hard to judge in language or vision, where those relations are rarely specified precisely enough to define a candidate internal algorithm. Arithmetic offers a cleaner setting. We study a Transformer trained on base-digit extraction: given $N$, $B$, and $D$, it must report the coefficient of $B^D$ in the base-$B$ expansion of $N$. The closed-form solution, $\lfloor N/B^D \rfloor \bmod B$, provides explicit candidate algorithmic intermediates. Across three seeds, the model reaches 99.83% exact-answer accuracy on held-out number-base intersections, establishing reliable task competence. Linear probes decode the intermediates, making staged arithmetic computation plausible. translated_title: 被表征不等于被计算：对Transformer中候选算法中间量的因果检验
translated_abstract: 结构化提示需要根据任务相关的关系来整合各个组成部分。在语言或视觉领域，由于这些关系很少被精确地定义到足以指定候选内部算法的程度，因此往往难以判断网络是如何实现这种整合的。算术提供了一个更干净的实验环境。我们研究了一个在进制数字提取任务上训练的Transformer：给定 $N$、$B$ 和 $D$，模型必须报告 $N$ 的 $B$ 进制展开中 $B^D$ 位的系数。闭式解 $\lfloor N/B^D \rfloor \bmod B$ 提供了明确的候选算法中间量。在三个随机种子上，模型在留出的数值进制交集上达到了99.83%的精确答案准确率，确立了可靠的任务能力。线性探针能够解码这些中间量，使得分阶段的算术计算看起来是合理的。随后的因果测试则将“表征”与“使用”区分开来：在从以 $D$ 为输入的流到输出位置的局部化通路内……（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 本文以进制数字提取任务为平台，通过因果干预实验发现线性探针可解码的候选算法中间量并不等同于模型实际计算所使用的量，从而在Transformer中严格区分了“被表征”与“被计算”。
en_tdlr: Using causal interventions on a digit-extraction Transformer, this paper demonstrates that candidate algorithmic intermediates decodable by linear probes are not necessarily what the model actually uses in computation, rigorously disentangling "represented" from "computed."
